ranked_targets.description: Confirm whether SAM3DBodyEstimator.process_one_image accepts any keypoint/pose hint beyond bboxes/masks.
ranked_targets.finding: NO. Read the vendored source directly: /home/preto/data/vaila/sam_3d_body/sam_3d_body/sam_3d_body_estimator.py's process_one_image(img, bboxes=None, masks=None, cam_int=None, det_cat_id=0, bbox_thr=0.5, nms_thr=0.3, use_mask=False, inference_type='full') exposes exactly bboxes/masks/cam_int as external guidance -- no keypoint or pose-hint parameter. There IS an internal keypoint-prompt refinement mechanism (models/decoders/keypoint_prompt_sampler.py, meta_arch/sam3d_body.py's _get_keypoint_prompt/_one_prompt_iter/run_keypoint_prompt), but it is a TRAINING-time iterative self-refinement loop: _get_keypoint_prompt reads batch['keypoints_2d'], which is ground-truth annotation data set only by the training dataset loader. The inference-time batch builder prepare_batch() (data/utils/prepare_batch.py) never sets batch['keypoints_2d'] at all. Repurposing this path at inference would mean reconstructing an unsupported internal batch field and bypassing self.training gating -- an unsupported, fragile modification to vendored upstream code, not a stable API.
ranked_targets.decision: Guidance mechanism is scoped down to BBOX TIGHTENING ONLY, computed client-side in vaila/sapiens2_3d.py from Sapiens2's 308 keypoints, before calling process_one_image(bboxes=..., masks=...) exactly as sam3dinov3.py already does. This must be documented explicitly in the new module's docstring so the feature is never oversold as 'keypoint-guided mesh regression' -- it is 'keypoint-tightened bbox + existing mask-conditioned mesh regression'.

Guidance CSV: 1000/1000 (100%) person-frames guided; num_keypoints_used per id averaged 258-271 out of 308 (far above the min_guidance_keypoints=4 threshold) -- the mechanism engages substantially and passes its own IoU sanity check on essentially every frame of this clip.
ranked_targets.evidence_reprojection_vs_independent_det: Novel cross-check devised for this run (not pre-specified in the loop doc, added because no ground-truth 2D exists for this clip): compared each run's reprojected MHR70 2D keypoints (shoulders/hips/knees/ankles) against Sapiens2's OWN independently-computed COCO17-indexed 2D keypoints (Sociopticon-308's first 17 follow COCO ordering per vaila_sapiens.py's SAPIENS_MID_HIP_KPT_IDS comment) for the same anatomical joints, per frame/person. Mean pixel distance: baseline=15.931 px, guided=15.936 px, delta=+0.005 px (n=1000 frame-person comparisons each) -- statistically negligible; per-id deltas all within +/-0.04 px. Interpretation: on this clip, bbox tightening does NOT change SAM 3D Body's 2D localization accuracy relative to an independent 2D detector, even though the box itself is 24-50% smaller in area.
ranked_targets.caveat: This clip is a clean, well-tracked, unoccluded scene -- exactly the case where SAM3's own bbox is already good, so it is the weakest possible test of whether tightening ever *matters*. It does NOT exercise the motion-blur/partial-occlusion cases the guidance mechanism is meant to help with (per the module docstring's own reasoning for why Sapiens2 keypoints could correct a loose SAM3 box). ids 0/1/3 have implausibly small bbox areas (~1100-2500 px^2, i.e. ~35-50 px per side in a 1920x1080 frame) despite passing the segment-length plausibility check -- a reminder that plausible segment lengths are necessary but not sufficient evidence of a genuinely-tracked person; the monocular mesh regressor's body-shape prior can produce an anatomically 'plausible' body from a near-noise crop. id 2 (bbox ~19-14k px^2, most stable segment lengths, std <=0.002 m) is the most likely candidate for the actual tracked athlete; id 4 is the next most likely (largest box, more motion).

lessons: sam_3d_body's process_one_image has no external keypoint-prompt hook at inference time; only bboxes/masks/cam_int. Do not attempt to wire Sapiens2 keypoints into the model's internal keypoint_prompt_sampler machinery -- it depends on ground-truth batch fields the inference path never populates.

rec3d_todo fixture currently has no pre-generated processed_sam3sapiens2_*/processed_sam3dinov3_* directories -- tier-3 evidence requires a fresh GPU run of the front end, unlike the sibling rec3d-mesh-blender-loop's fixture state.

Randomly-sampled synthetic keypoints in a unit test can make a deterministic-looking assertion flaky when the IoU sanity check is in the loop -- with only 4 random points the derived bbox can shrink enough that IoU vs a much larger SAM box dips under threshold. Fixed by using explicit deterministic corner keypoints sized comparably to the SAM box in the one test targeting the score-threshold boundary specifically (not the IoU check, which has its own dedicated tests).
Companion CSVs (not modifying a shared writer's schema) are a good, low-risk pattern any time new information needs recording without touching a schema another pipeline already depends on.

On a clean, well-tracked, unoccluded clip, SAM3's own mask-derived bbox is already good enough that a 24-50% tighter Sapiens2-guided crop makes no measurable difference to SAM 3D Body's 2D accuracy -- the real differentiator for this feature would be motion-blur/partial-occlusion frames, not clean ones. Future validation on a harder clip would be the natural next data point, not required for this loop's own closure.
